contradictions.topic: Windows Arm64 Flutter: deployment target vs host SDK

claim_a.text: Flutter's supported-platforms page lists Windows Arm64 as a deployment target.

claim_b.text: Flutter's only Windows SDK assumes an AMD64 host and runs on Windows Arm64 hosts under emulation; the issue to ship a native Arm64 SDK remains open at P3.

contradictions.strategy_tried: scope distinction (host tooling vs deployment target)
contradictions.resolution: Both hold: Windows Arm64 is a supported Flutter *target*, but no native Windows Arm64 *host* SDK ships; on an Arm64 Windows machine the Flutter tool runs under x64 emulation. A scaffold contract must record 'Flutter host on win-arm64 = emulated x64 tooling' and must not claim native host support.
contradictions.label: inferred
contradictions.audit_trail: curated by stage-06 agent from verified stage-05 claims

contradictions.topic: Rust Tier 1 aarch64-pc-windows-msvc vs dependency toolchain needs

claim_a.text: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, i686-pc-windows-msvc and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc are Tier 1 with host tools.

claim_b.text: ring's BUILDING.md requires both the VS 2022 C++ ARM64 build tools and clang components for aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.

contradictions.strategy_tried: scope distinction (compiler/std guarantee vs C-dependency build requirements)
contradictions.resolution: Rust's Tier 1 guarantee covers rustc, cargo and std; it does not cover crates with C/assembly build scripts. ring (used via rustls/reqwest in Axum/Tauri stacks) additionally needs clang on aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, and the request to drop that was closed as not planned. Windows ARM64 support must be verified per dependency, not inferred from the Rust tier table.
contradictions.label: inferred
contradictions.audit_trail: curated by stage-06 agent from verified stage-05 claims

contradictions.topic: Meaning of 'Tier 2' across Node.js and Rust

claim_a.text: Node.js Tier 2 platforms have full test coverage and test failures block releases, but binary releases may be delayed by infrastructure issues.

claim_b.text: Rust Tier 2 targets are guaranteed to build but the test suite is not executed, so produced binaries might not work.

contradictions.resolution: 'Tier 2' is not comparable across projects: Node.js Tier 2 (Windows arm64) still runs the full test suite and blocks releases on failures, whereas Rust Tier 2 runs no tests. Tier labels must be quoted with their project-specific definition in any support matrix.
contradictions.label: inferred
contradictions.audit_trail: curated by stage-06 agent from verified stage-05 claims

contradictions.topic: Invoking .cmd/.bat from Node without a shell

claim_a.text: Node.js documents invoking .bat/.cmd via spawn with the shell option as not recommended (DEP0190), offering exec or spawning cmd.exe with the script as argument instead.

claim_b.text: Since the CVE-2024-27980 fix, Node.js errors with EINVAL when a .bat or .cmd file is passed to spawn/spawnSync without the shell option.

contradictions.strategy_tried: recency (2026 API docs supersede the 2024 advisory's shell:true workaround)
contradictions.resolution: The 2024 advisory suggested { shell: true } for sanitized input; current docs deprecate that pattern (DEP0190). Every documented route to a .cmd/.bat goes through cmd.exe. A 'no shell' tooling contract therefore cannot invoke npm.cmd/npx.cmd/flutter.bat directly; it must resolve real executables (node.exe plus the package's JS entry, cargo.exe, dart.exe) or treat cmd.exe /c as an explicit, argument-validated exception.
contradictions.label: verified
contradictions.audit_trail: curated by stage-06 agent from verified stage-05 claims

contradictions.topic: Minimum Windows version for Tauri 2 apps

claim_a.text: Tauri 2 prerequisites list Windows 7 and later as a supported system.

claim_b.text: The Rust windows-msvc targets require Windows 10 or higher for client installs (Windows Server 2016+ for servers).

contradictions.strategy_tried: unresolved by authority (score gap 10 < 20) and recency (both current); reconciled by scope as an inference
contradictions.resolution: Inference: binaries built with current stable Rust *-windows-msvc targets have a Windows 10 floor, so a scaffold on a current toolchain should declare Windows 10+ regardless of Tauri's broader Windows 7 statement. Not checked by building/running on Windows 7 in this run.
contradictions.label: inferred
contradictions.audit_trail: curated by stage-06 agent from verified stage-05 claims
